summary: Benioff argues Salesforce is fundamentally strong despite the SaaS re-rating — $46B revenue, $16B+ cash flow, massive buyback — and that AI/agents create unprecedented new capabilities for the business, making the stock undervalued relative to fundamentals.
quote: We'll do over $46 billion this year, more than $16 billion in cash flow. We have more than 83,000 employees... I think it's one of the largest in history. Yeah, we were, we want to buy back as much as we can.

summary: Chamath argues that high-end enterprise software like Salesforce is safe from AI disruption — companies with deep C-suite relationships and strong net dollar retention are positioned to 'crush' as the market re-rates back and enterprises need trusted partners to deploy AI ROI.
quote: The high end of the market where Marc operates, where the large monoliths operate is quite safe... who has the best relationships, meaning they're inside the CXOs and the C-suite... Those guys I think are positioned to crush.

summary: Benioff describes Anthropic as a 'rocket ship' that correctly bet on coding agents and is now the clear leader, with Salesforce spending ~$300M on its tokens annually — a trajectory he says will not stop.
quote: Have you seen Anthropic? I mean, it is a rocket ship. That will not stop because you can use this product to do these incredible, amazing things.

summary: Chamath is skeptical of Anthropic's deployment-company deal economics, arguing paying $4B at a 17.5% guaranteed preferred return to compete with established consultancies like EY and Deloitte doesn't make mathematical sense given what those firms trade at.
quote: You have to put in $4 billion, you get all of these folks, you gave them a 17.5% preferred guaranteed return. For what? Essentially to stand up a competitor to Ernst Young, Andersen, Deloitte, PwC, Cognizant... that doesn't actually

scoreNote: Explicitly named as his choice for the next year
summary: Jason picks Apple as his top choice for the next year, citing its unmatched hardware footprint, the path to running local AI models with privacy advantages, and M-series chips enabling 10x employee productivity — making it best positioned among AI platform players.
quote: I think Apple's my choice for the next year.

summary: Chamath questions Apple's ability to pivot if a new AI-driven form factor disrupts the current device paradigm, noting its 30-40 years of process optimization may be a liability if the nature of the device changes entirely.
quote: Apple is incredible, but that's the product of 40 years, 30 years of meticulous process optimization. What do you do if the form factor is totally different and the nature of the device is different? How do you pivot that organization?

summary: Friedberg argues Google has a real opportunity to own the AI assistant interface by integrating Gemini across its personal data ecosystem (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Photos) and G Suite enterprise, calling it a 'formidable competitor' and a 'kickass product' once the flywheel gets going.
quote: Google has a real chance to kind of own that assistant interface... I think Google Assistant is gonna end up being kind of a real kickass product once they get this flywheel going.

summary: Friedberg notes that OpenAI struggles to maintain long-term partnerships, citing the breakdown of its Apple deal as evidence of a pattern — 'there doesn't seem to be a lot of long-term partnerships with OpenAI.'
quote: This— there doesn't seem to be a lot of long-term partnerships with OpenAI.

summary: Chamath argues the US should sell chips to China precisely so Nvidia wins the market rather than ceding ground to Huawei — a direct competitive argument for Nvidia's long-term chip dominance.
quote: Sell the chips. And the reason we should sell the chips is we want NVIDIA to win. We do not want to give enough oxygen for Huawei to then all of a sudden emerge and have a version of a chip that works.

summary: Chamath argues the low end of the SaaS market is 'basically finished' with no safe space, while AI-driven re-rating has compressed multiples across the sector to levels he's never seen before.
quote: I think the low end of the market is basically finished. I think there, there is no safe space.

summary: Chamath views a16z's political spending as a deliberate, strategically sound business move to grow its AUM toward $1 trillion and become the next Blackstone — describing it as 'an incredible feat' and 'a juggernaut of a business.'
quote: They're marching towards a trillion. They're going to be the next Blackstone, which I think is an incredible feat, and they're building a juggernaut of a business.
